answer: Each identity registers one vine cutting and locks a 70-credit bond. It is dipped in a nectar feed and marked with a sable ink serial binding cutting, batch, and time. After rooting, an auditor re-measures root length and feed level and recomputes growth from the vine-rooting table. A shortfall over 10 percent, a reused serial, or a borrowed cutting burns the bond. The first filing costs 36; the kth fake costs 36+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6030 and 1000 fakes cost 3,033,000. Rented cuttings fail because they share root histories and filed serials. An honest grower pays 36 once.
